## Executive briefing
- Two lead investment stories qualified this week: Bloomsbury’s ACOTAR launch cycle (ORANGE, 68/100) and NeeDoh scarcity with GAIN look‑through (YELLOW, 59/100).
- Bloomsbury’s ACOTAR #6 posted 958,195 U.S. hardcovers in week one (Circana BookScan via Publishers Weekly) and #7 is dated for January 12, 2027—material for FY26/27 and with a near‑dated catalyst. ([www2.publishersweekly.com](https://www2.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/publisher-news/article/101707-maas-s-latest-acotar-novel-sells-nearly-1-million-copies-in-first-week.html))
- GAIN’s September‑quarter 10‑Q (filed Nov 9) shows Schylling (NeeDoh) preferred equity marked up to $77.9M FV and $17.0M term debt outstanding (SOFR+11.0%, 14.7% cash), making Schylling ≈6.6% of portfolio FV—NAV‑relevant plus ongoing interest income. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1321741/000132174126000022/gain-20260930.htm))
- PS5 “shortage” chatter is real only for the premium PS5 Pro SKU in GTA VI/Black Friday week; standard PS5 remains broadly available. We classify this as a low‑materiality, short‑lived monitoring signal, not a lead. ([tomsguide.com](https://www.tomsguide.com/gaming/playstation/ps5-pro-restocks-updates-and-news))

- PS5 Pro stockouts (SKU‑specific): Evidence needed to move up—sustained, multi‑week U.S. out‑of‑stock at MSRP for base PS5 Slim Disc/Digital across major retailers, or Sony revising guidance citing component constraints (vs. demand seasonality).
